description:
Analysis code, harmonisation and transportability audits, and the de-identified single-centre validation cohort for a Glasgow Coma Scale-free long-term mortality model in critically ill patients with acute brain injury.

What is included. The full analysis pipeline (cohort description and missingness, model development with 28 predictors, external validation, recalibration, and the revision-round audits): aetiology-code leakage sensitivity analysis (including the joint deletion of those indicators together with the Charlson index, 28 → 20 predictors, and its paired DeLong comparisons, in scripts/91_leakage_sensitivity_v9.py and results/leakage_sensitivity_v9.json), GCS-component increment audit, calibration-slope epsilon-dependence audit, bootstrap confidence intervals for calibration metrics, harmonisation/transportability variants, NWICU vasopressor-extraction forensic audit, and the NWICU cohort descriptives. Every audit writes a machine-readable JSON result file; the results/ directory holds those files, including v8_figure_number_manifest.json, which registers every number printed inside every figure together with the JSON path it was derived from. v8_panel_provenance.json records, for every panel used by the eight composite figures, its generating script, dependencies, hash and modification time, and adds number manifests for the four internal panels that previously had none.

Figure provenance. A timestamp cannot prove that a figure was drawn from the current analysis, because a composite assembled from stale panels is still newer than those panels. 82_panel_pixel_repro.py therefore compares every panel, and all eight composite figures, against the output of an independent regeneration of the same generator, at the level of decoded pixels, and records a pixel hash that is independent of PNG metadata; results/panel_pixel_repro.json holds the per-file verdicts, and the one documented exception (a panel written by two scripts from different data vintages, unused by the figures) is named explicitly. results/v8_panel_provenance.json also carries an explicit count identity separating the panels the figures actually use from any panel tested but not used.

Severity scores. The SOFA / OASIS / SAPS-II head-to-head is computed from the official mimiciv_derived tables (first_day_sofa, oasis, sapsii), not from a re-implementation. 81_official_score_provenance.py records that the local database stores no DDL provenance at all, so the build commit cannot be recovered and is not claimed; equivalence is established instead by exact identities — the published total equals the sum of the coalesced component scores and the published probability follows the official logistic formula (including the SAPS-II log term) for all 94,458 rows of both tables — together with the two branch behaviours a re-implementation typically misses. The upstream revision compared against is pinned by blob SHA in results/official_score_provenance.json.

GCS comparability. results/gcs_increment_audit.json records, under comparability, that the GCS-free, total-GCS and motor-component models were fitted on the same held-out set with identical labels, imputation medians and scaling, so that the two reported AUC increments are directly comparable rather than merely similarly labelled.

What is not included. Patient-level source data (PhysioNet data-use agreements forbid redistribution of the source data and of objects derived from it, e.g. extracted cohort CSVs and trained model files) and the manuscript/appendix production scripts. The de-identified local cohort (n = 239 rows) is included. See the README for the exact inclusion/exclusion boundary and how to obtain the rest.
notes: Companion analysis repository. The de-identified local cohort file is released under CC BY 4.0; the code is MIT.
